archetype.instructions: Which kind of dashboard does the request ask for?

criteria.executive_overview: A broad summary of the business: revenue, orders, margin, customers; a few headline numbers and one or two trends
criteria.sales_performance: Sales results in depth: revenue and orders over time, by product category, department, brand
criteria.customer_acquisition: Where customers come from and who they are: signups, traffic sources, demographics, geography
criteria.product_merchandising: What is selling: categories, brands, margins, returns, product mix
criteria.fulfillment_operations: Shipping and delivery: order status, days to ship and deliver, distribution centers
criteria.web_engagement: Website behaviour: sessions, events, funnel steps, conversion, browsers
criteria.inventory_health: Stock levels and inventory value by warehouse and category

time_window.instructions: Which time window does the request imply? If none is stated, pick the standard window for the kind of dashboard.

criteria.last_30_days: Last 30 days, the last month, recent weeks: a short-term operational view
criteria.last_90_days: Last 90 days, the last quarter, the last three months: recent with enough history for a trend
criteria.last_12_months: Last 12 months, the past year, trailing year: the standard window for trends and seasonality
criteria.year_to_date: Year to date, YTD, since January 1st of the current year
criteria.all_time: All time, all history, everything available (about two years)

grain.instructions: At which time granularity should trends be plotted?

criteria.day: Daily, by day: for short windows or operational monitoring
criteria.week: Weekly, by week: smooths daily noise over a quarter or more
criteria.month: Monthly, by month: the standard for yearly views and executives
criteria.quarter: Quarterly, by quarter: only for multi-year, high-level views

compare_prior.instructions: The reader wants each number compared with the previous period (growth, change, versus last period).

density.instructions: How much should be on the dashboard?
criteria: A few headline numbers and one chart
A balanced overview: several numbers and a handful of charts
A dense analytical view with many charts and a table

criteria.executive: Leadership: wants a few clear numbers and the overall trend
criteria.analyst: Analyst: wants breakdowns, comparisons and the ability to dig in
criteria.operator: Operations staff: wants current status and many signals at once

mode_preference.instructions: Does the request state a visual mode preference?

criteria.light: The request asks for a light, white or bright look
criteria.dark: The request asks for a dark look, a wall screen or night use
criteria.no_preference: The request says nothing about light or dark

wants_geo.instructions: The request is about geography: countries, states, regions or a map.

wants_breakdowns.instructions: The request asks to break results down by a category (by product, by channel, by segment, etc.).

legend.0: A few headline numbers and one chart
legend.1: A balanced overview: several numbers and a handful of charts
legend.2: A dense analytical view with many charts and a table

layout.instructions: Which layout template fits this dashboard?

criteria.kpi_row_grid: KPI row + grid: Headline stat tiles across the top, then charts packed into a grid below. The conventional overview dashboard.
criteria.hero_focus: Hero focus: One large main chart with stat tiles down the left side and a few small supporting charts. When one trend is the whole story.
criteria.two_column: Two columns: Every chart at half width in two even columns, stat tiles inline. Balanced comparison of several equally important views.
criteria.narrative: Single column narrative: Full-width tiles stacked in reading order, one idea per screen height. For a report that is read top to bottom rather than scanned.

theme.instructions: Which theme preset fits the audience and any stated mode preference?

criteria.daylight: Daylight (light, comfortable): Light, neutral, comfortable spacing. The safe default for analysts working at a desk.
criteria.midnight: Midnight (dark, comfortable): Dark surface with the same palette re-stepped for dark mode. For wall screens, dark-mode users and evening monitoring.
criteria.boardroom: Boardroom (light, spacious): Light, spacious, larger type, fewer tiles per row. For executives and presentations where a few numbers must be readable from a distance.
criteria.ops_dense: Ops dense (dark, compact): Dark, compact, small type, many tiles per screen. For operators watching many signals at once.

criteria.compact: Abbreviated figures such as $1.2M or 34K; scan-friendly
criteria.precise: Full figures such as $1,234,567; when exact values matter

gridlines.instructions: The reader benefits from horizontal gridlines to read values off the charts.

direct_labels.instructions: The reader wants values written directly on the bars and line ends rather than reading the axis.

sort_breakdowns.instructions: How should categories be ordered in breakdown charts?

criteria.by_value: Largest value first; for ranking questions
criteria.natural: The category's own order (alphabetical, or ordered bands); for lookup and comparison

connector.instructions: Which data connector should back this dashboard, given the environment?

criteria.static_snapshot: Static snapshot: Pre-aggregated JSON cubes extracted from BigQuery and embedded in the dashboard. Works offline, no credentials, data as of the snapshot date.
criteria.bigquery_live: BigQuery live: Run each tile's query against bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce at view time. Always current, needs a billable GCP project and credentials. (not yet implemented)
criteria.csv_upload: CSV upload: The viewer supplies a CSV export matching the cube schema. For sharing a dashboard with people who lack warehouse access. (not yet implemented)
